contradict_spans: Cardiac troponin I level was 25 ng/mL
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of paroxysmal chest pain and ECG findings of ST-segment elevation and depression suggest vasospastic angina, which can be a cause of acute coronary syndrome.

support_spans: paroxysmal chest pain

contradict_spans: total occlusion of the right coronary artery (RCA) and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery (LMCA)
candidates.why: The patient's episodic chest pain and transient ST-segment elevation are characteristic of Prinzmetal's angina, a rare condition caused by coronary artery spasm.
candidates.protected_reason: Prinzmetal's angina is a rare diagnosis that may be overlooked in favor of more common causes of chest pain, and its consideration is protected to ensure that this potentially treatable condition is not missed.

total occlusion of the right coronary artery (RCA) and subtotal occlusion of the left main coronary artery (LMCA)
contradict_spans: repeated ECG reveals sinus bradycardia (46 beats per minute), Q-wave amplitude deepening, ST-segment falling back to equipotential line, and T-wave inversion in lead III
